app.title: ExoScout
app.summary: A person types the catalog measurements for one transit observation into a two-column form, which starts filled with an example. They can clear a field to mark a measurement as missing. When they press classify, the values are checked and a frozen, pre-trained classifier gives a binary call (planet-like or false-positive-like), an uncalibrated score shown as a percentage and a bar, and the fixed threshold it used. A note says how many missing values were imputed, and an expandable section explains how to read the score.

task.text: Get a quick planet-like or false-positive-like call from a frozen trained classifier for one transit observation, entered as catalog measurements.

data.text: A single tabular observation of a fixed set of numeric catalog features (transit geometry and host-star properties), any of which may be missing, scored by a saved model.
data.item: one catalog observation: a row of numeric measurements for one candidate

stage.text: screening catalogued transit candidates for likely false positives, before manual vetting

mechanism.text: A form with one field per model feature sends a single observation to a saved classifier pipeline; the result area below shows the binary call, the score as a number and a bar against a fixed threshold, a warning for imputed missing values, and an expandable note on how to interpret it.

field.text: machine-learning classification of transit candidates in exoplanet astronomy

workflow.name: classify one item with a frozen trained model

steps.here: Type the measurements for one observation into a two-column form that starts filled with an example; clearing a field marks that measurement as missing.
On submit, an all-empty form is refused, and each value must be numeric and finite. Physical quantities such as period, duration, depth, temperature and radius must also be positive.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: The saved pipeline (median imputation with missingness indicators, then a random forest) scores the observation, and the score is compared with the frozen threshold to give a binary label.

steps.step: read the call and how confident it is
steps.here: A green or amber banner shows planet-like or false-positive-like, with the uncalibrated score as a percentage metric, a progress bar and the threshold in a caption.

steps.step: check the caveats on the result
steps.here: A warning counts how many values were imputed. An expander explains that the score is not a calibrated probability, and a footer states the model version, feature count and threshold.

distinctive: The model, its feature order and its decision threshold are frozen in a saved artifact, so the interface can only apply the classifier and cannot retrain or tune it.
Missing measurements are allowed on purpose: an empty field becomes a missing value that the pipeline imputes, and the result reports how many were filled in.
Input checks use physical constraints: some quantities must be strictly positive, and all must be finite.
The score is labelled uncalibrated, with an explicit note that the tool reproduces catalog dispositions and does not confirm discoveries.

parts.title: Observation features form
parts.summary: One labelled text field per model feature, with units, help text and example defaults, laid out in two columns with a single classify button.

parts.title: Input validation
parts.summary: Turns blank fields into missing values, refuses an all-empty form, and rejects values that are non-numeric, not finite, or not positive where the quantity must be.

parts.title: Frozen model inference
parts.summary: Loads and caches the saved pipeline artifact, checks it has the keys it needs, scores the observation and applies the stored threshold to get a label.

parts.title: Model output
parts.summary: Shows the binary call as a coloured banner, the uncalibrated score as a percentage metric and progress bar, and the threshold it was compared with.

parts.title: Caveats and model notes
parts.summary: Warns how many missing values were imputed, explains in an expander that the score is not a calibrated probability, and gives the model version and threshold in a footer, with a disclaimer at the top.
